content:
We got a list of templates. Need the one that matches SN2 halide displacement forming secondary amine. Look at entries: first entry reaction_id 759948 seems complex with B(O)O etc not SN2. Second entry reaction_id 22361: retro_smarts_template '[C:2]-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[#7:3]-[C:4]-[c:5]1...>>O=[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[C:2])-[#7:3]-[C:4]-[c:5]...' This seems like amide formation? Not SN2.

Third entry reaction_id 195396: retro_smarts_template '[C:2]-[NH;D2;+0:1]-[c:3]>>O=C(-O-C-c1...)-[N;H0;D3;+0:1](-[C:2])-[c:3]' That's maybe acyl substitution.

Fourth entry reaction_id 1341356: retro_smarts_template '[C:6]-[NH;D2;+0:7]-[c;H0;D3;+0:2]...>>C-C(-C)-N(-C-[CH3;D1;+0:1])-C(-C)-C.Cl-[c...].[C:6]-[NH2;D1;+0:7]' This looks like SN2 where a Cl attached to aromatic carbon is displaced by amine? The template shows a Cl attached to aromatic carbon and amine leaving group? The product side: [C:6]-[NH;D2;+0:7]-[c...] (C-N bond) and the other side: [C:6]-[NH2;D1;+0:7] (the nucleophile). The template seems to represent SN2 where a halide (Cl) attached to aromatic carbon is replaced by amine. That matches our case: we have a side chain Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3. The carbon attached to N is part of aromatic ring, likely originally a chloride. So template ID likely corresponds to this entry. Need template ID. The search result didn't include template IDs, only reaction_id and template_hash. We need to retrieve template by ID. Possibly template ID is the template_hash? Or there is separate ID. The tool get_template expects template_id string. We might use template_hash as ID. Let's try get_template with that hash.

Pick the fourth entry's template_hash: '5af915c72612c934e4be5d67dbd24eb2f8214e4d73afe062d2517cf163121b01'.
